  A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1A)         Mr. Arjun, aged 35, decides to follow stricter financial discipline while ensuring he spends quality  
  time with his family. He plans to invest ₹15,000 at the end of every month in an investment account  
  until he turns 50 years old (a total of 180 payments).  
  For the first five years (from age 35 to 40), the investment earns 20% nominal interest compounded  
  quarterly. After the fifth year, the return is expected to reduce to 10% per annum, as he shifts to  
  safer investment options.  
  Beginning at the end of his 40th year, Arjun starts to withdraw ₹2,40,000 every year to fund family  
  vacations, while continuing his regular monthly investments until he turns 50. The final withdrawal  
  is also made at the end of his 50th year.  
  Assuming all deposits and withdrawals occur at the end of their respective periods, determine the  
  total amount that will remain in Arjun's account immediately after the withdrawal at age 50.

  1C)           A manufacturing company incurred an initial loss of ₹10,00,000 due to environmental non-  
  compliance. With corrective actions and improved pollution control systems, the loss amount is  
  expected to be reduced by a fixed amount each year over the next five years. The total estimated  
  future worth of loss over this five-year period is ₹35,00,000. Assuming that the reduction in losses is  
  uniform (i.e., the same each year) and that the company uses a discount rate of 10% per annum to  
  evaluate the time value of money, determine the annual reduction in loss value.

  2A)              A Ltd. depreciates its equipment at 10% p.a. on declining balance method. On 2019 the  
  undepreciated amount of the equipment was ₹8,50,000 (Original Cost ₹12,00,000). Determine the  
  book value of the asset in the years 2022 and 2023. Also, in 2025 if the machine is expected to be (4)  
  sold for ₹2,30,000 what will be its sunk loss or capital gain.  
  
  2B) Your company needs to choose between two punch press models for purchase. The financial details for each (3)  
  are summarised below, and both machines have a 5-year lifespan with a residual scrap value of \$15,000.  
  Using a 12% interest rate, perform a present worth analysis for a study period of four years to determine the  
  more economical option.  
  Model A: Initial cost is \$250,000. It has an annual operating cost of \$4,000 and generates an annual benefit  
  of \$89,000.  
  Model B: Initial cost is \$205,000. It has an annual operating cost of \$4,300 and generates an annual benefit  
  of \$86,000.  
  Assume the market value of the asset is equal to the salvage value and the company adopts straight line

  2C)               The Harmony Constructions Pvt. Ltd. is bidding for a government housing project aimed at  
  constructing low-cost homes for needy families in a suburban region. As per the tender  
  conditions, the company must design, construct, and maintain the housing colony for the next 100  
  years (assume n=∞). The project engineers have estimated the following details: The initial cost  
  of design, materials, and construction is estimated at ₹6,50,00,000. The cost of developing  
  essential infrastructure such as roads, drainage, and water connections within the colony is  
  estimated at ₹75,00,000. The annual maintenance cost (for building repairs, painting, and  
  common area maintenance) is expected to be ₹8,00,000 in the first year and will increase by  
  ₹80,000 every year due to ageing of structures and inflation. After 10 years, a major renovation  
  (including roof replacement and repainting) will be required, costing ₹60,00,000, and it will recur  
  every 10 years thereafter. After 15 years, the company plans to adopt a new maintenance material  
  technology at a cost of ₹40,00,000, which will reduce the annual maintenance cost to ₹3,00,000  
  per year, with no further increase. Assume a MARR of 8% per annum and determine the total  
  amount Harmony Constructions Pvt. Ltd. should quote in its proposal.

  5A)              Three types of drill bits can be used in a certain manufacturing operation. A bright high-speed  
  steel (HSS) bit is the least expensive to buy, but it has a shorter life than either gold oxide or  
  titanium nitride bits. The HSS bits will cost \$3,500 to buy and will last for 3 months under the  
  conditions in which they will be used. The operating cost for these bits will be \$2,000 per month  
  and salvage value is \$2,000. The gold oxide bits will cost \$6,500 to buy and will last for 6 months  
  with an operating cost of \$1,500 per month and salvage value is \$4,000.                             (4)  
  The titanium nitride bits will cost \$7,000 to buy and will last 12 months with an operating cost of  
  \$1,200 per month with salvage value of \$3,000.  
  At an interest rate of 15% per year, compounded monthly, which type of drill bit should be used  
  based on Annual Worth analysis?

  Lakhs, Rs. 2 Lakhs, Rs. 1.75 Lakhs, Rs. 1.5 Lakhs, Rs. 1.25 Lakhs for years seven to eleven respectively.
